rationale: Both independently rediscover the human reviewer's top High-severity finding (legacy v1 checkpoints mis-parsing as the v2 codec config), but Y also nails the exact root cause of linyueqian's other High comment (stream-slot leak on abort, correctly identifying the req_id vs external_req_id space mismatch) where X only finds a loosely related leak via a different, less precise mechanism. Y also correctly flags the Seed-TTS WER PCM-fallback issue that linyueqian explicitly raised as a real concern, whereas X explicitly asserts that same fallback is 'safe,' directly contradicting ground truth and hurting its precision. Both miss several human comments entirely (cumulative/delta rewind bug, ceil-division audio_codes_lengths truncation, cleanup-of-saved-audio and debug-log cleanup asks, generalizability/preprocess-function suggestions), and both are heavily loaded with speculative-but-plausible extra findings that inflate volume without matching ground truth. Both are highly actionable with concrete file:line citations and suggested fixes, but Y's better hit-rate on the two most severe human-flagged issues and its lack of a contradicted claim give it the edge.
